**Slug:** `pe719-root-enumeration` — `research/backward/pe719-root-enumeration.md`

**The reduction.** An S-number is a Kaprekar-type number with "2 parts" generalised to "2 or more parts". The catalogued form is OEIS **A038206** (roots `m`; its square values are **A104113**), and the key structural fact is that an S-number is indexed by its root, so

$$T(N)=\sum_{m=2}^{\lfloor\sqrt N\rfloor} m^2\cdot [S(m)]$$

with `S(m)` = "the digits of `m²` split into ≥2 nonempty blocks summing to `m`". At `N=10^12` this turns a `10^12`-scan into a `10^6`-scan. Neither OEIS sequence carries a closed form (`base` keyword), so enumeration of roots is the intended method, not evaluation of a formula.

**Gaps.** Five total; I checked each against the (empty) claim ledger and `search_claims`, so "discharged" here means discharged by a derivation in the file or a cited source note, not by a claim id:

- `G-root-identity` — **discharged** (unique positive root bijection; 0 and 1 admit no two-part split).
- `G-mod9-filter` — **discharged** (casting out nines: `m ≡ digit-sum(m²) ≡ m² (mod 9)`, so `9 | m(m−1)` and since `gcd(m,m−1)=1`, `m≡0 or 1 (mod 9)`); cross-checked against the A038206 comment.
- `G-split-predicate-correct` — **open**. `next`: DFS over cut positions with a partial-sum prune, unit-tested against A038206 roots ≤ 100.

Archivist verdict on the three parallel PE 719 candidates: adopted TWO (not one) — candidate/01 (DFS over digit-block boundaries with overshoot pruning) as the genuinely-distinct winner, plus candidate/02 (memoized digit-DP over position+remaining-sum) as the second required independent method. Both correct on all four reference values (41333, 10804656, 6222187932, 128088830547982). Caution for the next turn: NEITHER adopted candidate left a run-log (code/out/candidates_dfs.log, candidates_digitdp.log absent) — their agreement is by in-source assertion and code inspection, corroborating the already double-verified reference values, not by a fresh full-size execution. Candidate/03 (meet-in-the-middle) committed nothing on its branch and was rejected. Running the two adopted candidates to confirm would close this gap.

Candidate 03 (meet-in-the-middle over prefixes) was initially rejected as "committed nothing" — that was wrong: it was read before its branch committed. It has since committed code/candidates_mitm.py plus a complete full-size run log: T(10^4)=41333, T(10^6)=10804656, T(10^9)=6222187932, T(10^12)=128088830547982 (count 406), all worked examples reproduced, unity with brute force on every root in [2,5000], and a verified mod-9 filter. It is the only candidate with a finished 10^12 run (01 reached 10^11, 02 only 10^9). Now adopted as code/candidates_mitm.py.

PE719 settled: T(10^12)=128088830547982, verified three independent ways. (1) code/solution.py memoized digit-partition recursion, (2) code/verify_bfile.py summing squares of OEIS A038206 b-file roots with 2<=m<=isqrt(N) (independent of the recursion), (3) code/candidates_mitm.py meet-in-the-middle over prefix/suffix sum sets, which completed a full 10^12 run (count 406 S-numbers; 0 brute-force mismatches on every root in [2,5000]; validated mod-9 filter m≡0 or 1 mod 9). All three reproduce T(10^4)=41333, T(10^6)=10804656, T(10^9)=6222187932. Files: code/solution.py, brute.py, verify_bfile.py, candidates_{dfs,digitdp,mitm}.py; answer claim t-final-answer is in the claims ledger.

The repunit witness identity m(m−1) = Σᵢ bᵢ(10^{Lᵢ}−1) has a cyclotomic-basis refinement nobody in the loop stated: 10^{Lᵢ}−1 = Σ_{d|Lᵢ} Φ_d(10), so m(m−1) = Σ_d c_d Φ_d(10) with c_d = Σ_{i : d|Lᵢ} bᵢ. For k=2 this is degenerate (c_d = b₁ for all d|L, giving Iannucci's unitary-divisor correspondence); for k≥3 the coefficient vector (c_d) is a genuinely new free object, and the cyclotomic gcd structure gcd(Φ_a(10),Φ_b(10)) is the divisibility lever on m(m−1) — the k-block analogue of the divisor enumeration that made two-block Kaprekar numbers tractable. Adopted as research/approaches/repunit-linear-representation.md.
